question: Where did DRDO successfully conduct the maiden flight-tests of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) on 23 August 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha Coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the maiden flight-test of the **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS)** on **23 August 2025**.
 
• The test was carried out from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)**, **Chandipur**, located off the **Odisha Coast**. This facility is the primary site for evaluating the performance of India's missile systems and flight vehicles.
 
• The flight-test was aimed at demonstrating the **vertical launch capability** and the integrated functioning of the weapon system against a high-speed, **low-altitude aerial target**.
 
• The **IADWS** mission achieved all its technical objectives, with the missile following the predicted trajectory and successfully intercepting the target. The performance was monitored by various **Range Sensors**, such as **Radar**, **Electro-Optical Tracking System (EOTS)**, and **Telemetry** stations.
 
• This successful trial confirms the operational efficiency of the system's **propulsion**, **control systems**, and **guidance algorithms**, marking a significant milestone in India's indigenous air defense capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, **DRDO** is the premier research and development wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It is headquartered in **DRDO Bhavan**, **New Delhi**, and operates a network of over **50 laboratories** across the country.
 
• Its primary mission is to empower the **Indian Armed Forces** with state-of-the-art indigenous **defence technologies** and systems, ranging from **missiles** and **combat vehicles** to **radars** and **electronic warfare** systems.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS):**
 
 
• The **IADWS** is designed to provide **short-range** protection to vital assets against a variety of aerial threats, including **UAVs**, **fighter aircraft**, and **cruise missiles**.
 
• It utilizes a **canister-based launch system**, which allows for rapid deployment and provides **360-degree coverage** to the user.
 
• The system integrates advanced **Active Radar Seeker** technology to ensure high precision during the terminal phase of engagement.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Test Range (ITR) Chandipur:**
 
 
• Located in the **Balasore district** of **Odisha**, **ITR Chandipur** is India’s most important missile testing ground.
 
• Its unique geographical location provides a wide **flight corridor** over the **Bay of Bengal**, making it ideal for testing long-range and short-range **surface-to-air** and **surface-to-surface missiles**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Features:** The **IADWS** features sophisticated **Electronic Counter Counter Measures (ECCM)**, which allow it to operate effectively even in the presence of intense **electronic jamming** from enemy assets.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** The development of the **IADWS** is a critical part of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) initiative, aiming to reduce dependence on foreign-made **Integrated Air Defence** solutions.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** The deployment of such indigenous systems significantly enhances the **Indian Navy** and **Indian Air Force's** ability to respond to **low-altitude** threats in **maritime** and **border regions**.
 
• **Collaborative Development:** The system's development involves multiple **DRDO labs**, including the **Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL)** and the **Research Centre Imarat (RCI)**, highlighting the collaborative nature of Indian **defence engineering**.
